privacy.legal-lead.003: How TransGuru handles data and how you can manage permissions, files, and privacy requests.
privacy.legal-date.004: Last updated and effective: October 30, 2026Applies to: TransGuru website and Android app
privacy.li.007: 2. Website visits and local interactions
privacy.p.017: This policy applies to the TransGuru website and TransGuru Android app provided by Saleslify Technologies ("we", "us", or "our"). It explains how we handle information related to you. Contact us about privacy at devs.pesafy@gmail.com.
privacy.p.018: TransGuru helps you transfer WhatsApp or WhatsApp Business data between devices that you are authorized to use. Chats move directly between devices. We do not use a cloud relay server for chat transfers. Website visits, third-party technology, and support requests that you choose to send may involve the other processing described below.
privacy.p.019: WhatsApp, Google Play, GitHub, and any email or sharing service you select are operated by their respective providers under their own policies. This policy does not replace the choices you must make in system permission prompts or during specific migration steps.
privacy.p.021: This is a static website. We do not place ads, analytics, tracking pixels, account registration, or data submission forms on it. We do not set analytics or marketing cookies. Fonts and images are served by the website itself.
privacy.p.022: Checklist choices stay in the current page memory. They are not submitted to us or written to cookies or browser storage, and they disappear when you refresh or close the page. Language is represented by the URL path. When you switch languages on the homepage, the selected transfer direction may be kept in a URL parameter. The URL contains no chat content or encryption keys, but is sent to the hosting provider as part of a normal page request.
privacy.p.023: When the website is published with GitHub Pages, GitHub logs and stores visitor IP addresses for security. This hosting activity does not mean that we collect your chat content. See GitHub Pages data collection and the GitHub Privacy Statement. When you open an external link, the destination receives a normal network request.
privacy.p.025: The app accesses a device, file, or content only after you start the relevant feature and grant the required permissions. A chat backup may contain personal information about you and other chat participants. Confirm that you are authorized to transfer this data.
privacy.caption.026: Data types, purposes, and processing locations
privacy.td.030: Chat text, account numbers and contact identifiers, group information, photos, videos, voice messages, files, call records, and other message content in the backup
privacy.td.031: Read and preview the selected backup, convert its format, and restore supported content on the destination device
privacy.td.032: Your source and destination devices; local intermediate files may be created during processing
privacy.td.033: Backup passwords, 64-character encryption keys, and key screenshots that you choose
privacy.td.034: Unlock, validate, or decrypt the selected backup, and recognize a key in a screenshot on the device
privacy.td.035: Keys and passwords are used for local processing. The original screenshot remains under the control of your gallery or file location. See Section 6 for chat working files.
privacy.td.036: Device model, system version, USB pairing information, connection identifiers, and local network session information
privacy.td.037: Identify the connected device, establish a connection, check compatibility, and maintain the migration session
privacy.td.038: The local device, connected device, and local migration session
privacy.td.039: Backup paths, file lists, migration progress, account previews that may include account numbers, contact names, and recent message summaries, device identifiers, and error information
privacy.td.040: Show progress, resume the previous migration, and diagnose failures
privacy.td.041: Local migration directories, state files, and diagnostic logs
privacy.p.042: We do not use chat content for advertising or sell chat data. The current app does not require a TransGuru cloud account, so migration backups are not stored on our account servers.
privacy.p.044: Permissions depend on the migration direction and system version. You can review or revoke permissions in Android settings. A related feature may stop working after you revoke access. Denying notification permission alone does not block migration.
privacy.td.048: File and media access, including All files access
privacy.td.049: Find the selected WhatsApp backup, read media, and write migration output and recovery files. This system permission has broad access. Grant it only after you understand its purpose.
privacy.td.051: After you approve the system prompt, connect to and identify an iPhone for backup or restore transfer
privacy.td.053: Scan the connection QR code shown on the other phone during Android-to-Android migration
privacy.td.054: Nearby Wi-Fi devices, Wi-Fi and network state, and location permission on older Android versions
privacy.td.055: Create a local hotspot or join a migration network. Android 12 and earlier may require location permission for related Wi-Fi features. We do not use it to track your location.
privacy.td.056: System photo picker or gallery selection
privacy.td.057: Read only the key image that you select when you choose screenshot recognition
privacy.td.058: Gallery background-process management on older systems
privacy.td.059: After the fallback gallery picker is used, the app may ask Android to stop that gallery app's background process so it does not take control of the USB connection. This does not grant access to photos you did not select.
privacy.td.061: Show progress during migration and help the connection and background task continue
privacy.td.062: Installation-status checks and system uninstall flow for specified apps
privacy.td.063: Check whether WhatsApp, WhatsApp Business, or related system services are available, and open an uninstall or install flow that you must confirm when required
privacy.p.064: Visiting the website does not give us access to your phone's camera, files, USB devices, or location. The app and operating system request phone permissions in context.
privacy.p.067: Migrations involving an iPhone use a USB cable. Android-to-Android migration uses a local hotspot created by the app or the same Wi-Fi network, and the session is encrypted. The recipient is the other device that you select and connect. Scan QR codes only from trusted devices, and do not process chat backups on an untrusted phone.
privacy.p.069: The app includes Google ML Kit on-device text recognition to read a backup key from a screenshot that you select. The image and recognition result are processed on the device and are not sent to Google servers by the recognition feature.
privacy.p.070: ML Kit may still send technical information about the component to Google, including the device model and system version, app package and version, a per-installation identifier, recognition performance, input and output sizes, configuration, feature events, and error codes. These diagnostic and usage metrics are separate from your screenshot and chat text. Google states that these metrics are sent over HTTPS and that ML Kit may contact its servers to maintain the component. See ML Kit Terms and Privacy, ML Kit data disclosure, and the Google Privacy Policy. You can enter the key manually instead of using screenshot recognition.
privacy.p.072: The app stores diagnostic logs on the device to troubleshoot connection or migration problems. When you choose to share them, the app opens the system share sheet and you choose the recipient. We do not receive logs automatically through this feature. The store build redacts specified sensitive log fields, but file names, device information, or other context may still contain personal information. Review the content before you send it.
privacy.p.073: When you email us, we process your email address, message, and attachments that you choose to provide so we can answer your question or handle a privacy request. Do not send backup passwords, complete keys, chat databases, private chat screenshots, or unnecessary identity documents. Your email or sharing service also processes the content under its own policy.
privacy.p.075: To support migration resume, some backups, preview information, and intermediate data are stored in Android shared storage. They may remain after you uninstall the app or clear its app data. They may include decrypted chats or media. Delete them after you verify the migration.
privacy.p.076: Backup and working files may be in the Download/.transguru/ migration directory. WhatsApp manages restored data in its own directories. Some flows clean the workspace when they finish or when you start a new task. Files may remain if a flow is interrupted or cleanup fails. We do not promise that all files are deleted immediately and automatically when migration finishes.
privacy.li.077: After you confirm that chats and media are complete on the new phone, use Delete all migration data in the app settings to clean the app's public migration directory. This does not delete data already restored to WhatsApp.
privacy.li.078: You can also use the system file manager to clean the public migration directory, other copies of original backups, key screenshots, and files you copied manually. Confirm each path before deletion to prevent data loss.
privacy.li.079: Use the system Clear storage action or uninstall the app to remove private app state, pairing data, and local logs. Check shared directories and exported copies separately.
privacy.li.080: Emails and log copies sent to us or another party are not deleted when you clean the phone. To request action on support information that we received, contact the email address in Section 10.
privacy.p.081: When you delete migration data, the app first moves the working directory to a hidden trash area, then deletes its files in the background. If the process stops, the next app launch may need to continue cleanup. This is normal file deletion. It is not secure erasure that overwrites the storage medium.
privacy.p.082: Local logs rotate by file size and are not a permanent, complete activity history. We keep support information that we receive only while it is needed to handle the request, make necessary follow-up contact, or meet applicable legal requirements. We delete or de-identify it when it is no longer needed. Google, GitHub, and email providers manage their data under their own policies. You can exercise your rights with the relevant provider.
privacy.p.084: You can choose not to start a migration, not to use screenshot recognition, to deny optional permissions, or to revoke permissions in system settings. Stopping a transfer, revoking a permission, or disconnecting a device may cause the current task to fail. Follow the app's instructions to stop safely, then check the source backup and destination device.
privacy.p.085: You can review and delete files on your devices. For personal information that we actually hold because of a support request, you may email us to request access, correction, deletion, restriction, withdrawal of consent, or other rights available under applicable law. We ask only for the information needed to verify and handle your request, and we respond within the time required by applicable law. Withdrawal does not affect processing that was lawful before withdrawal.
privacy.p.086: Because chat backups are mainly on your devices, we cannot remotely read, retrieve, restore, or delete those local files for you. The current service has no TransGuru cloud account, so there is no separate cloud-account deletion process.
privacy.p.088: We reduce risk through system permissions, device confirmation, encrypted local-network sessions, and redaction of sensitive log fields in the store build. Some migration flows must create recoverable plaintext working data. Encrypted transfer does not mean that every file on disk is always encrypted. Protect device passcodes and do not place backups or keys in untrusted shared locations.
privacy.p.089: TransGuru is for people who are authorized to manage the relevant devices, accounts, and backups. It is not directed to children. Minors may use it only when local law and third-party age requirements permit, with any required guardian consent. Contact us if you believe a minor's information was submitted to us improperly.
privacy.p.090: Third-party services may process technical or support data outside your country or region. Their policies describe processing locations and safeguards. This does not cause the migration feature to upload chat backups to our servers.
privacy.p.092: We may update this policy when features, data processing, or legal requirements change, and we will update the date on this page. If a change adds a new use of personal information, a new recipient, or another material change, we will provide notice on the website or through an appropriate app notice. We will obtain consent again when applicable law requires it. You can always access this policy from the website footer.
